persona: Simulated beginner beatmaker new to DAWs, aiming for a 30-second hip-hop-style sketch using audio and a VST MIDI instrument with mouse input only.

outcome.status: Completed composition, project save, WAV export and MIDI export through visible mouse controls; file contents await independent coordinator verification.
outcome.composition: Stock Circuit rhythm audio repeated across four clips with the final clip shortened, plus a manually drawn 12-note C-minor-oriented phrase in Rill Lab Sine repeated across four MIDI clips, final clip shortened. Tempo retained at 112 BPM.
outcome.playback: First attempt showed 51 plug-in/render failures. Following the suggested stop/restart recovered visible playhead movement and both track meters. No audio was auditioned.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Blank-area MIDI prompt, instrument assignment, Pencil note drawing, marquee selection, Duplicate, and export defaults made the main task achievable without keyboard input. Opening MIDI editing took an extra discovery step.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Dark layout, teal waveforms, compact transport, and visible MIDI notes felt cohesive and readable. The piano-roll grid was less immediately legible than the arrangement.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most edits responded promptly and the complete attempt took about six minutes, but the first playback error and several-second native dialog appearance interrupted the flow. This is a session impression, not a hardware benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Only modest confusion overall: double-clicking a MIDI clip did not visibly open it, selected clip trimming affected one clip, and error details gave little explanation. Context menus and retry instructions allowed recovery.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: Audio arrangement, VST MIDI drawing, duplication, naming, project save, and both requested export types were available. This brief task did not evaluate broader production features.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the new MIDI clip did not visibly open the editor. Right-click exposed Edit notes and successfully opened it.
findings.recommendation: Make opening a selected MIDI clip more discoverable, for example with a visible Edit notes action or a clear double-click affordance.

findings.observation: The first Play produced a plug-in/render error with 51 failures. Details repeated the warning plus diagnostics without explaining which operation failed. Stop and restart, as instructed, recovered moving playback and both meters.
findings.recommendation: Identify the failing plug-in or operation and expose a direct retry action; preserve the helpful stop/restart guidance. Diagnose this specific lab failure before generalizing to other plug-ins.

findings.observation: Dragging the edge of one of two selected final clips trimmed only that clip. I then trimmed the MIDI clip separately. The resulting arrangement was 30.134 seconds rather than exactly 30.
findings.recommendation: Show which selected clip edges will change during a trim and expose an exact end-time readout while dragging.

findings.observation: Pencil dragging immediately created notes, displayed their names, and extended the clip. A C-sharp note outside C natural minor appeared red, which helped me notice and move it.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the scale coloring and note labels; a brief explanation of red out-of-scale notes would help new users.

findings.observation: Rename project included a mouse-operated keyboard, including Select all and Space. The resulting title became the default project, WAV, and MIDI filenames.
findings.recommendation: Retain this mouse-only naming path and consistent filename defaults.

positives: The blank arrangement area explicitly advertised double-click for MIDI and led directly to the instrument library.
The instrument library clearly identified Rill Lab Sine as a VST3 instrument and offered Assign instrument.
Marquee selection and Duplicate repeated audio and MIDI together; Fit showed the whole arrangement.
Pencil drag feedback and automatic clip expansion made basic note entry quick.
The on-screen keyboard made a custom project name possible using only the mouse.
WAV export summarized arrangement duration, format, and effect tails; MIDI export showed an explicit completion status.
limitations: Agent simulation, not a human participant or human research.
No audio capture was auditioned; hip-hop style was an intent, not a verified listening judgment. No sound-quality claim.
Only the supplied stock audio and Rill Lab Sine native VST were exercised; no conclusions about third-party plug-ins.
Software graphics, timer-paced virtual audio, 60 ms lab buffering, and 1024-frame requests at 48 kHz limit performance conclusions.
A window manager was absent; native file-dialog positioning and short appearance delays may be environment-specific.
Project contents and output file contents were not inspected during the task. Artifact paths come from visible save/export dialogs; the coordinator verifies independently.
WAV export was observed in progress and later Re-export last WAV was enabled, but its completion toast was not captured. MIDI completion was captured explicitly.
The starter project supplied the audio rhythm; this attempt did not test audio import, recording, or drum sound design.
